items.prompt: Given the head of a linked list, reverse the nodes in groups of k and return the new head; a final group shorter than k stays as it is.
items.why: 'Reverse' + blocks of a linked list → In-place Reversal, run once per block with two reconnections. Dummy-head splicing alone doesn't turn arrows around.

items.prompt: Given the head of a linked list and k, rotate the list to the right by k places.
items.why: Rearranging a linked list in place by rewiring next pointers → the In-place Reversal family (close the list into a ring, cut it at length − k). Two Pointers' rotate-by-reversals works on arrays, not lists.

items.prompt: Return true if a singly linked list reads the same forwards and backwards, using O(1) extra space.
items.why: To compare without a stack you must walk the second half backwards → reverse it in place. Fast/slow only finds where the second half starts, and a stack costs O(n).

items.prompt: Given the head of a linked list, return the middle node; with two middles, return the second.
items.why: Finding a position without changing any links → Fast & Slow Pointers. Nothing is reversed.

items.prompt: Merge two sorted linked lists into one sorted list by splicing their nodes.
items.why: Splicing two lists in order with a dummy head → Linked List Basics. Pointers are redirected, but nothing is turned around, and with only 2 lists there's no heap.

items.prompt: Reverse the characters of a string in place, given as an array of characters.
items.why: An array has indices at both ends → swap from the outside in with Two Pointers. There are no next pointers to flip.

items.prompt: Given the head of a linked list and positions left <= right, reverse the nodes from position left to position right in one pass.
items.why: Reverse a sub-list → the prev/curr/next flip run (right − left + 1) times, plus two reconnections at the borders.
